**Do not edit this file.** As in the data collection repository, the 0.75x scale, link masses
(body 0.78 kg + 4 x 0.005 kg rotors = 0.8 kg), rotor joint locking and zeroed initial velocities are
applied by the asset config (`assets/drones.py`), not stored in the USD.

## Original structure

- defaultPrim `/vehicle` (articulation root, self collision on), Z up, metres.
- `/vehicle/body`: rigid body, 1.5 kg with a stored `diagonalInertia` (0.029125, 0.029125, 0.055225)
  kg·m² from the PX4 Gazebo Iris. This must be cleared when the mass is overridden so the inertia is
  recomputed from the shape. The collider is one body+arms mesh (convex decomposition).
- `/vehicle/rotor0..3`: propeller rigid bodies (no mass set), `rotorN/jointN` revolute about z.
- Narrowest waist width at x = 0 is about 105 mm at full scale, about 79 mm at 0.75x. The gripper
  opens 107 mm, so the drone must be scaled.

## Files used by drone_grasp_rl

| File | What |
|---|---|
| `iris_0p75.usda` | **PhysX** entry (`assets/drones.py` `IRIS_USD_PATH`). References `iris.usd` and overrides scale 0.75, masses (body 0.78 kg, rotors 4 x 0.005 kg), explicit inertia and center of mass (values PhysX computes from the scaled colliders, so PhysX and Newton use the same), rotor joints locked by +-0.01 deg limits (MuJoCo rejects an empty 0..0 range), zero initial velocities, and `MaterialBindingAPI` on the prims whose source binding lacks it (USD warned on every load). Keeps the original `convexDecomposition` body collider, as in the data collection repo. Hand-written. |
| `iris_0p75_newton.usda` | **Newton** entry (`IRIS_NEWTON_USD_PATH`): `iris_0p75.usda` with `iris_collision.usda` on top. Hand-written. |
| `iris_collision.usda` | Generated by `scripts/build_drone_collision.py`. Turns off collision on the original body mesh (it stays visible) and adds 30 invisible convex-hull pieces from a fixed CoACD decomposition (seed 0), bound to a physics material with friction 1.0 and torsional friction 0.02 m (MuJoCo makes one contact point per finger-piece pair; without torsional friction the dropped drone pivoted between the fingers). `--material_only` rewrites only the material. |

`drone_grasp_rl.physics.DRONE_USD` picks the entry per backend.

Why two colliders:
- Newton decomposes a `convexDecomposition` collider with CoACD at load time. The pieces differ between runs, and a
  near-zero-volume piece makes MuJoCo fail with "mesh volume is too small". So Newton gets fixed pieces.
- PhysX keeps its own decomposition because the grasp depends on the exact underside of the waist. With the fixed
  pieces, the grasped drone pitched about 14 deg after the motor stop (the judge allows 10 deg). With the original
  collider it turns 1-3 deg and the close on the drone stops at 16.2 deg, as in the data collection repo
  (rotation up to 2.1 deg, 16.4 deg).
- Waist width at drone x = 0, 0.75x: mesh 78.4 mm, fixed pieces 83.0 mm, PhysX decomposition 81.3 mm (old repo).
  The gripper opens 107 mm and the grasp criterion is 87 mm or less.
